key_insight: In simulated radiology workflows, rules plus an LLM checker reduced pooled high-severity error episodes from 19.4% to 13.2%, but did not eliminate them.
clinical_relevance: Pre-action safeguards may improve the reliability of AI-generated radiology documentation, but residual errors warrant continued oversight.
method: Evaluated six tool-using LLM agents across 48 synthetic, radiologist-reviewed scenarios and 91 total variants.
Compared permissions only, deterministic rules, and rules plus a locally run LLM checker across 1,638 episodes.
Measured episodes with at least one executed high-severity violation.
evidence_signal: Exploratory pooling across agents found a 6.2-percentage-point reduction with rules plus an LLM checker versus permissions only (95% CI: 3.0–9.5 points), without a detectable decrease in task success.
watch_item: These simulation findings do not establish real-world effectiveness, and 64%–68% of blocked actions would not have caused a violation, raising revision-workload concerns.
paper_title: Safeguarding Agentic AI in Radiology Workflows: A Multimodel Evaluation of Rule-based and Large Language Model-based Verification
